events.title: The martyrdom of St. Cyprian of Carthage
events.shortBlurb: The bishop and great writer of the African Church was beheaded before his people in the persecution of Valerian…
body: St. Cyprian, bishop of Carthage and one of the foremost Latin writers of the early Church, had guided his flock through persecution and plague and through the bitter controversy over the readmission of those who had lapsed. When the persecution of the Emperor Valerian struck the leaders of the Church, Cyprian was arrested and sentenced.

On 14 September 258 he was led out and beheaded near Carthage in the presence of a great crowd of the faithful, having first blessed God and provided for the executioner's fee. His memorial is kept on 16 September together with Pope Cornelius, whom he had defended a few years before and who had himself died for the faith in exile.
